children: A federal auction of 23 geothermal leases on more than 71,000 acres in Idaho attracted $7.8 million in winning bids, led by Chicago-based power developer Invenergy, according to sale documents published by the U.S. Bureau of Land Management.
Bighorn Resources LLC of Fort Worth, Texas, emerged as the largest aceage winner, securing seven parcels on about 22,900 acres for $2.26 million.
Invenergy bid $2.64 million for four parcels on about 17,600 acres and submitted the auction's largest single winning bid, roughly $1.2 million for a parcel in Owyhee County.
The highest per-acre bid came from Bennett Creek Resources LLC of Houston, which paid $810 an acre for a parcel in Elmore County.
The auction's total topped that of two geothermal lease sales in Idaho in 2025, underscoring growing competition for geothermal resources as a source of round-the-clock clean power.
